description.zh: 將人體工學融入最日常的備料動作，以拇指、食指、中指的自然夾持姿勢為核心，讓施力方向與手部肌肉走向一致。底部快拆式刀盤可自由切換削皮刀片或磨板，一個握把應對多種廚房需求。
description.en: Seamlessly blending ergonomics into daily meal prep, ERGO PEEL centers on the natural pinch grip of the thumb, index, and middle fingers, aligning applying force with hand anatomy. Featuring a quick-release base, it easily switches between a peeler and a grater—handling diverse kitchen tasks with just one handle.

text.zh: 從日常備料的施力痛點出發，分析拇指、食指、中指的自然夾持姿勢，鎖定削皮動作的人體工學問題。
text.en: Started from the strain of daily meal prep — analyzing the natural pinch grip to pinpoint the ergonomic problem in peeling.

text.zh: 以多輪草模快速測試夾持姿勢與施力角度，反覆修正握把型態，讓施力方向與手部肌肉走向一致。
text.en: Rapid mockups tested grip posture and force angles, iterating the handle form until force aligned with hand anatomy.

text.zh: 以 SolidWorks 完成 3D 建模與快拆刀盤機構，產出實體成品，並以簡報表板完整呈現設計論述。
text.en: Modeled in SolidWorks with a quick-release blade mechanism, delivered the physical product and presentation boards.

reflection.zh: 人體工學的部分研究還不夠深入，產品表達也不夠清楚——造型應該要讓人看一眼就懂、就會用。
reflection.en: The ergonomic research needs more depth, and the product isn't communicating itself clearly enough. The form should be intuitive — understandable and usable at first glance.

description.zh: 秉持「形隨機能」的精神，Lumina 剝離冗餘修飾，將家具精煉為純粹的幾何體塊。透過玻璃的透、鋼材的剛、混凝土的重，在理性結構中尋求平衡。幾何發光核心不僅是視覺焦點，更是溫暖空間與功能的匯集點。
description.en: Upholding the spirit of "form follows function," Lumina strips away redundant ornamentation, refining the furniture into pure geometric volumes. Through the transparency of glass, the rigidity of steel, and the gravity of concrete, it seeks a harmonious balance within a rational structure. The geometric illuminating core is not only a visual focal point, but also a convergence point where warmth and functionality meet.

reflection.zh: 最大的工藝挑戰在於材料與製程的限制。這次經驗讓我體會到，設計不只是追求理想中的完美，更是在色彩、材質、工藝與製造限制之間，靈活尋求最佳解的過程。
reflection.en: The biggest challenge lay in the limits of materials and fabrication. This taught me that design isn't just about pursuing theoretical perfection — it's about agile problem-solving within the real constraints of color, material, craft, and manufacturing.

text.zh: 從玻璃、鋼材、混凝土三種材料的物理特性出發，尋找幾何體塊之間理性而溫暖的平衡，讓發光核心成為視覺與功能的匯集點。
text.en: Started from the physical character of glass, steel, and concrete, seeking a rational yet warm balance between geometric volumes with the light core as the focal point.

text.zh: 原訂以 3D 列印製作全透明燈罩，但支撐材痕跡難以打磨消除。將限制轉化為設計機會，改以幾何花紋紋理呈現，光線穿透後意外創造出層次豐富的光影效果。
text.en: Originally planned a fully transparent 3D-printed shade, but support-material marks proved impossible to fully polish out. Turned the constraint into an opportunity — a geometric pattern texture that creates rich light-and-shadow layering instead.

text.zh: 完成鋼材、玻璃、混凝土的組裝與發光核心整合，並以表板與實體拍攝呈現最終設計論述。
text.en: Assembled the steel, glass, and concrete elements with the integrated light core, and presented the final design through boards and product photography.

subtitle.zh: 攝影課程・靜物與場景

description.zh:
攝影課的練習，分成兩種完全不同的題目。

一組是我自己塗裝的微縮模型場景。難處不是打光，而是怎麼讓一個放在桌上的東西看起來像真的存在。把相機降到場景裡小人的視線高度，用淺景深模擬人眼的距離感，畫面就會從「一個模型」變成「一個地方」。

另一組是棚拍靜物。從零架設燈光，反覆調整光位與光比。最花時間的是金屬——銀壺、搖酒器這類反光材質會把整個棚，包括燈具和自己，都照進去，得靠柔光與遮光一點一點把不該出現的東西擋掉，才留得住乾淨的高光。

從自己動手做出來，到把它拍成別人看得懂的樣子——這兩件事其實是同一條線。
description.en:
Two very different assignments from a photography course.

One is a miniature scene I built and painted myself. The difficulty here isn't lighting — it's making something sitting on a table look like a place that exists. Dropping the camera to the eye level of the figures, using shallow depth of field to imitate how distance reads to the human eye, and the frame stops being "a model" and becomes "somewhere".

The other is studio still life. Building the lighting from scratch, adjusting position and ratio over and over. Metal took the longest — silver pots and cocktail shakers reflect the entire studio, the lights and you included, so it becomes a slow process of diffusing and flagging until only the clean highlights are left.

Making the thing, then photographing it so other people understand it — those turn out to be the same line of work.

text.zh: 先用單燈找出物件的立體感從哪裡來，再逐步加入輔助光與反光板，控制光比不讓陰影死黑。
text.en: Started with a single light to find where the form reads, then added fill and reflectors to control the ratio and keep shadows from going flat black.

text.zh: 拍微縮模型時把相機降到小人的視線高度，用淺景深製造距離感，讓場景看起來像實際存在的空間。
text.en: For the miniatures, dropped the camera to the eye level of the figures and used shallow depth of field to build a sense of distance, so the set reads as a real space.

text.zh: 以 Photoshop 統一整組照片的色調與亮度，讓兩種題材看起來仍屬於同一組作品。
text.en: Unified tone and exposure in Photoshop so both subjects still read as one body of work.

reflection.zh:
最難的不是把東西拍清楚，是決定要讓人先看到哪裡。光可以強調，也可以隱藏，這跟做造型其實是同一件事——都在處理視覺的優先順序。

拍自己做的模型時感覺特別明顯：東西是我做的，但拍不好就沒人看得出我在意的地方在哪。

還在練，離腦中想要的畫面還有一段距離。
reflection.en:
The hard part isn't making things sharp — it's deciding what someone should notice first. Light can emphasise and it can conceal, which turns out to be the same problem as shaping a form: both are about visual priority.

Photographing something I made myself brought that into focus: I built the thing, but if it's badly shot nobody can tell which part I cared about.

Still practising. There's a gap between what I picture and what I get.
